answer: Rate-limited identity bonds: every new agent locks a refundable stake in a protocol vault, and the network admits only a fixed number of registrations per epoch. A Sybil operator who wants a nebula of a thousand fake agents must freeze a thousand bonds and wait many epochs for slots, while any clone caught later forfeits its bond. Honest agents get the deposit back at the dawn of their second month, so the cost lands almost entirely on the attacker.
